this_page: Builder work list. Not the product. An end user should never open this.
user_gets_today: Nothing they can use. The warehouse is empty, so there is no stock list.
user_gets_when_ready: A desktop screen. On the left they pick a universe, add conditions and choose a ranking. On the right they get the stocks that match, ranked, with the count that passed and the count that had no value. Plus a few named study blocks to start from. No advice, no forecast.
one_thing: Rules in, stocks out: universe, filter, rank on real data, shown on one desktop screen.
why: A short-term investor does not lack filters. They lack the next question worth asking, and every tool hands them knobs instead of an answer.

tasks.what: Repository foundation: working agreement, locked decisions, product and architecture documentation, query specification, Cursor rules, skills, role agents, contribution guide, continuous integration.
tasks.why: Sessions are paid. A repository that does not state its rules sends the next session down a path we already rejected.

tasks.what: Canonical warehouse schema and the metric catalogue, with reserved slots for weight, backtest and deploy.
tasks.why: The scanner cannot exist before the data has a shape, and the shape has to serve the whole path or we rebuild it.

tasks.what: Complete checkpointed harvest: every symbol and every index, resumable, idempotent.
tasks.why: Analysis quality is capped by coverage. Fill it once properly, then keep it current cheaply.

tasks.what: The query engine: universe, nested filter, rank and top N, with attribution for every removal.
tasks.why: This is the product. A rule goes in, a ranked list of real stocks comes out.

tasks.what: Desktop interface: operations on the left, results on the right, study blocks to start from.
tasks.why: The engine is useless to an end user without a screen that does not bombard them.
